provenance: New source translation; E3830-E3839 and E3920-E3929 reviewed.
context: Rod puzzle rewards a key; Cock Robin directs party to an heirloom box, with exact dial instructions. Gate Keeper and Key Master taunt party near a seal.
decisions: All numeric directions and puzzle clues preserved. Cock Robin explicitly male in source. Kaipers and Nameless Book are provisional terms. Cross-row sentences retain breaks.

translations.en: and something appeared!
It seems the order was wrong.
Then in what order should you insert them?
The only possible clues
were the messages paired with each rod.
The @3rRed Rod@0r and "Hope comes out last."
The @3rYellow Rod@0r and "One less than three."
The @3rBlue Rod@0r and "The squirrel goes for the walnut first."
Which order was correct?
A metallic click sounded, as though a lock had opened.
You gently lifted the lid. It opened easily.
Inside the box
was an exquisitely crafted @3rKey@0r.
A @3rkey@0r? What on earth is it a @3rkey@0r to?
There are tiny letters carved on it...
But this doesn't look like any script used today.
Is there nothing else?
Just to leave this @3rKey@0r behind,
they built such an elaborate mechanism?
That must mean this @3rKey@0r is extremely important.
I'll hold on to this @3rKey@0r for now.
I'd like @7rAnselm@0r to look at it too. Let's return to the tavern.
A human who appeared to be a thief was watching you.
They seemed to be deciding whether you were an enemy.
Looking at the face, you noticed a birthmark shaped like a little bird.
When you asked if he was @7rCock Robin@0r, he said yes
and lowered the weapon he was holding.
Cock Robin
I'm surprised to meet someone looking for me in a place like this.
What do you want?
Had his family kept something entrusted to them by @7rChu Lu Gah@0r?
If so, you had been asked to retrieve it.
You explained the request you had accepted.
Oh, that. An ancestor was given it hundreds of years ago.
You're welcome to it, but I don't have it on me.
It's hidden in a box right near the sign that says Kaipers.
The box has a combination dial. The number of turns opens it.
Three turns right, two turns left, then five turns right.
I'm glad I can finally return it.
It's a strange thing. Honestly, I didn't know what to do with it.
Give my regards to whoever sent you.
@7rCock Robin@0r vanished into the darkness once more.
You should look for the Kaipers sign
and find the box there.
You found an extremely sturdy box.
A round dial replaced the keyhole,
with a single button beside it.
Presumably, turning the dial
and then pressing the button would unlock it.
Could you remember how many turns @7rCock Robin@0r said
to make to the left and right?
Right 2, Left 3, Left 5
Right 3, Left 2, Right 5
Left 2, Right 1, Left 4
Left 3, Right 2, Left 2
You turned the dial and pressed the button.
But no matter how long you waited, the box showed no sign of opening.
That must not have been the right combination.
What had @7rCock Robin@0r said?
Try to remember once more.
Then the box opened with a quiet click.
Inside was an object wrapped in oiled paper and securely bound.
Undoing the string revealed a small book.
It had no title.
@7rAnselm@0r had said it was stolen from a demon.
Indeed, as if to confirm those words, a sinister aura
seemed to emanate from the book.
You decided to take this @3rNameless Book@0r back with you.
An eerie, oppressive atmosphere hung over the place.
You sensed something like a field of force there.
Faint rainbow light leaked out here and there,
so visibility was fairly good.
So, you finally made it.
I was sure you'd turn tail and run.
You've got some nerve, sticking around like this.
You'll be a pleasure to crush. Heh heh heh heh.
Do you know what this place is?
It's one of @7rChu Lu Gah's@0r seals on the gate to another realm.
Perhaps "gate to another realm" is hard for you to grasp.
When it opens, the monsters you call demons
